import pandas as pd

# Load source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_98/training_0.csv"

# Read Source4_98_0 twice as per the JOIN operation history
df_source0_a = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source0_b = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Perform the JOIN operation on PassengerId
# Both dataframes have the same schema, join on 'PassengerId'
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source0_a, df_source0_b, on="PassengerId", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Reorder and select columns to match the target schema:
# ['PassengerId': int, 'Survived': int, 'Pclass': int, 'Name': str, 'Sex': str, 'Age': float,
#  'SibSp': int, 'Parch': int, 'Ticket': str, 'Fare': float, 'Cabin': str, 'Embarked': str,
#  'Fare_x': float, 'Fare_y': float]

# The join will produce columns:
# PassengerId, Survived_x, Pclass_x, Name_x, Sex_x, Age_x, SibSp_x, Parch_x, Ticket_x, Fare_x, Cabin_x, Embarked_x,
# Survived_y, Pclass_y, Name_y, Sex_y, Age_y, SibSp_y, Parch_y, Ticket_y, Fare_y, Cabin_y, Embarked_y

# According to the target schema and example, we keep the left table's columns (without suffix) for all except Fare_x and Fare_y,
# which come from the join suffixes.

# Construct the final dataframe with correct columns and types
df_target = pd.DataFrame({
    "PassengerId": df_joined["PassengerId"].astype(int),
    "Survived": df_joined["Survived_x"].astype(int),
    "Pclass": df_joined["Pclass_x"].astype(int),
    "Name": df_joined["Name_x"].astype(str),
    "Sex": df_joined["Sex_x"].astype(str),
    "Age": df_joined["Age_x"].astype(float),
    "SibSp": df_joined["SibSp_x"].astype(int),
    "Parch": df_joined["Parch_x"].astype(int),
    "Ticket": df_joined["Ticket_x"].astype(str),
    "Fare": df_joined["Fare_x"].astype(float),  # This is the Fare from left table (same as Fare_x)
    "Cabin": df_joined["Cabin_x"].astype(str).replace("nan", pd.NA),
    "Embarked": df_joined["Embarked_x"].astype(str),
    "Fare_x": df_joined["Fare_x"].astype(float),
    "Fare_y": df_joined["Fare_y"].astype(float),
})

# Replace string "nan" with actual NaN for Cabin column
df_target["Cabin"] = df_target["Cabin"].where(df_target["Cabin"] != "nan", pd.NA)

# Save the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_98/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
